questions.question: Which eye protection is appropriate for a school activity with chemical-splash risk?
choices: Ordinary reading glasses alone
Contact lenses alone
A face shield without required goggles
Chemical splash goggles specified by the teacher

questions.question: What source describes a chemical's hazards and handling precautions?
choices: A periodic-table position alone
A Safety Data Sheet
The bottle's color alone
A student's prediction

questions.question: What should a student do if a laboratory instruction is unclear?
choices: Improvise a replacement procedure
Use twice the listed material
Ask the teacher before proceeding
Skip all protective equipment

questions.question: Which footwear is ordinarily appropriate for a school laboratory?
choices: Closed-toe shoes
Open-toe sandals
Bare feet
Footwear exposing the toes

questions.question: What should be done with long hair before working near laboratory equipment?
choices: Leave it loose near moving parts
Secure it away from equipment and materials
Hold it back only while reading instructions
Cover only the tips with gloves

questions.question: Who should supervise student laboratory work?
choices: The teacher or designated qualified instructor
Only another student
No one if written instructions exist
An observer unfamiliar with the activity

questions.question: How should laboratory chemical waste be handled?
choices: Always poured into a sink
Always mixed with other leftover chemicals
According to the teacher's designated disposal procedures
Always returned to stock bottles

questions.question: Why should food and drink be kept out of laboratory work areas?
choices: All food produces dangerous chemical reactions
Drinking always changes experimental temperature
Food replaces the need for cleaning
They can become contaminated or lead to accidental exposure

questions.question: Why should small spills and broken equipment be reported immediately?
choices: Only large accidents affect safety
Even small incidents can create hazards requiring appropriate action
Reporting is useful only after class ends
Students can identify every chemical by appearance

questions.question: Why should unused chemicals not be returned to a stock container?
choices: Stock chemicals always have unlimited purity
Returning chemicals makes the container lighter
All chemicals become harmless after one use
They may contaminate the shared supply

questions.question: Why is a clear, uncluttered work area important?
choices: It reduces contamination, spills, and trip hazards
It guarantees every experiment's hypothesis
It eliminates the need for supervision
It prevents all instrument uncertainty

questions.question: Why should glassware be inspected before use?
choices: Appearance establishes chemical purity
All glass is safe at every temperature
Cracks or damage can make it unsafe
Glass damage affects only the printed labels

questions.question: Why should students learn emergency-equipment locations before an activity?
choices: They should use all equipment without instruction
Equipment replaces every prevention measure
They need to follow trained emergency procedures promptly
Every emergency uses the same response

questions.question: Why are gloves not a replacement for proper hygiene and handling?
choices: They can become contaminated and must be used appropriately
Gloves eliminate all chemical hazards
Gloves make every substance safe to taste
Gloves guarantee no transfer to other surfaces

questions.question: Why should only teacher-authorized investigations be performed?
choices: Authorization makes any chemical harmless
Students cannot ask scientific questions
All alternative procedures are scientifically identical
Unreviewed changes can introduce unknown risks

questions.question: A student finds an unlabeled liquid. What should the student do?
choices: Identify it by tasting a drop
Avoid using it and notify the teacher
Mix it with another liquid to see what happens
Assume it is water because it is clear

questions.question: A beaker is chipped near its rim. What is the appropriate action?
choices: Report it and use teacher-approved replacement equipment
Use it because the damage is small
Hide the chip with a label
Repair it with any available adhesive

questions.question: During an activity, a student notices a small unknown spill. What is appropriate?
choices: Clean it immediately without identifying hazards
Leave it until the next class
Alert the teacher and follow the designated response
Dilute it with any nearby liquid

questions.question: A classmate proposes mixing leftover chemicals to avoid waste. Which response is appropriate?
choices: Mix them because all leftovers are compatible
Keep waste in the designated system and ask the teacher
Combine them only if their colors match
Return the mixture to an unused reagent bottle

questions.question: A student's gloved hands have handled chemicals. Before touching a phone, what should the student do?
choices: Wipe the gloves on clothing
Touch the phone because gloves prevent contamination
Add another pair of gloves without removing the contaminated ones
Follow instructed glove-removal and handwashing procedures
